## Analysis

Sol_0025 confirms that even whole-row/column destroy–repair cannot improve the `q=56`, `n=277` tensor incumbent. Together with sol_0024, this refutes both local cell moves and single-slice reconstruction as useful escape mechanisms. The plateau is therefore structural rather than an optimizer-temperature issue: improvements likely require simultaneous changes across both tensor axes. Earlier projection sweeps show geometry alone is insufficient, while the nonlinear embedding gain in sol_0023 remains the only recent progress. The next search should preserve that embedding but use coupled rectangular moves capable of reorganizing several interacting rows and columns at once.

## Next

Embed sol_0023 as an immediate atomic fallback, fix `q=56`, and run a 155-second large-neighborhood search that repeatedly selects `r,c ∈ {2,3,4,5}` rows/columns and replaces their induced cross (`r` full rows plus `c` full columns) using a width-32 beam over 128 correlated masks, followed by greedy cell refinement. Use seed `5026`, maintain `240<=n<=320`, exact-score every candidate, and checkpoint strict improvements atomically.
